01 / Traditional monitoring
At a traditional center, every detection becomes a clip for a human to review.
22 cameras across 3 sites. 3 human operators.
How it works
Traditional video monitoring runs object detection on each camera. People, moving vehicles and even wind-blown foliage become clips, and every clip goes to a monitoring center where a human operator reviews it for threats.
22 cameras across 3 sites
Every detection becomes a clip A retail store, employee lot and truck yard send activity for review.
Routine activity
Cashiers. Wind. Deliveries. Object detection flags activity without understanding why it is happening.
Legacy monitoring center
3 human operators Every clip needs their attention, including the routine ones.
02 / Peak hours
When activity spikes, the queue backs up and a real threat waits its turn.
20+ min #20 in line. The threat is still waiting for an operator to open it.
How it works
During busy periods, routine clips pile up faster than operators can clear them. A real threat waits its turn behind all of them, and it often takes 20+ minutes before an operator even opens it.
Incoming clips
The queue keeps growing Routine detections arrive faster than the three operators can review them.
Real threat · Site C
Catalytic converter theft A theft in progress waits behind routine activity.
Illustrative peak-hour backlog
#20 in line · 20+ min The threat is still waiting for an operator to open it.
03 / More bodies
The only way they can fix that is more bodies, so your price keeps going up.
You lose coverage. Lower quality. You pay more. In the meantime operators clear the queue as fast as they can and mute the cameras that seem low risk.
How it works
Monitoring centers can’t put more people in seats on demand. So they silence sites, offshore operators to developing countries, and charge more for extra alarms. None of it gets a real threat seen faster.
Silence busy sites
You lose coverage Muting noisy cameras reduces the queue by hiding activity.
Offshore the operators
Lower quality Cheaper seats do not add capacity on demand.
Charge for extra alarms
You pay more Overage fees do not get a real threat seen faster.
04 / Verdun
AI agents review every alarm first. They dismiss the noise, log what’s routine, and escalate what’s real.
0:38 A human sees the alarm in 0:38 in this example.
How it works
Verdun deploys AI agents that identify suspicious behavior, weigh the context, and reason about what they see. Only then do they pull up a live view and escalate to one of our human operators.
Glare on a store door
Dismiss Sees moving glare. Checks that the store is closed and no one is inside.
Truck at the loading dock
Log only Sees a truck backing in. Checks the scheduled overnight delivery.
Person cutting under a truck
Escalate · Voice down Checks that the yard is closed. Pulls live view; a human sees the alarm in 0:38 in this example.
05 / The result
An operator gets the clip, a live view, and your protocol on one screen.
<90 s Every alarm reviewed in under 90 seconds.
Book a demo
How it works
Because agents clear routine activity before it reaches a person, our operators only see what matters. Your alarms are always reviewed in under 90 seconds.
Legacy center · Peak hours
20+ minutes Routine alarms and real threats compete for the same operators.
Verdun
Under 90 seconds Agents review routine activity so real threats reach human operators.
The illustrated Verdun queue
1 alarm needs a human Wind and an employee leaving are dismissed. A scheduled delivery is logged. The theft is escalated.

02 / Verify
Understand the threat.
The context to know what actually matters.
Details
AI looks at every clip and decides whether it needs a human, based on what you want monitored at your site. One site might be set up for a person with a gun, another for a person loitering.
Environmental triggers and authorized activity are separated from real threats against your site’s protocol.
Motion alone isn’t a threat. Verdun checks what happened against your response protocol so an operator receives a verified incident with the context to act.
This camera’s protocol
Real product · Customer names changed
03 / Respond
Put response in motion.
Our operators aren’t bogged down trying to clear a queue, so they pay real attention to your property.
Book a demo
Details
Our human operators are active 24/7 to review alerts. They call the police, text you about what’s going on, and send you reports. You also get a text line into our monitoring center, so you can text us at any time.
When an agent escalates, the operator gets the clip, a live view, the agent’s assessment, and your protocol on one screen. They talk down intruders through on-site speakers, dispatch police or guards, and send your team an update the agent has already drafted.
Drafted by the agent
Technology
The entire picture. The power to act.
From the first signal to the final report. One platform connects detection, verification, and response across your sites.

Think of us less like a monitoring center and more like human enhanced AI analytics.

So we pit AI against AI. Our agents clear the noise. Our humans get what’s real and take action.

## Common questions | Verdun
URL: https://verdun.ai/faq

Common questions | Verdun
Skip to content
support@verdun.ai
Replay opening
Common questions
How Verdun works.
What is Verdun?
Verdun is a remote video monitoring service, backed by Y Combinator. AI agents review every alarm. Trained operators respond to real threats. We built the world’s most advanced monitoring center.
How is Verdun different from traditional video monitoring?
At a traditional center, every detection becomes a clip for a human to review. When activity spikes, the queue backs up and a real threat waits its turn. At Verdun, AI agents review every alarm first. They dismiss the noise, log what’s routine, and escalate what’s real.
How fast does an operator see a real threat?
Every alarm is reviewed in under 90 seconds. At a traditional center during peak hours, a real threat can wait 20+ minutes before an operator even opens it.
Can I choose what Verdun looks for?
Yes. Tell us what you want to look for. Our AI looks for it and our human operators act on it. Arming schedules and response rules reflect how each property operates.
What happens when there is a real threat?
Verified threats go to our operators, trained on your site’s protocol, for talk-down, dispatch, and notification. The operator gets the clip, a live view, the agent’s assessment, and your protocol on one screen. They talk down intruders through on-site speakers, dispatch police or guards, and send your team an update the agent has already drafted.
Are Verdun’s operators available around the clock?
Our human operators are active 24/7 to review alerts. They aren’t bogged down trying to clear a queue, so they pay real attention to your property.
What kinds of properties does Verdun monitor?
One console across commercial, multifamily, and industrial properties.
Does Verdun work with my existing cameras?
Give us your deployment details: your current VMS and your cameras. We hook up to your cameras and monitoring begins.
What if Verdun misses something?
If AI or human error causes a miss that leads to damage, we’ll reimburse you up to $20,000.
Can I try Verdun before switching?
If you have monitoring today and your deployment supports it, we’ll monitor side by side with your current provider for free. We agree up front on what counts. You can also start us at your next site with a 30 day pilot and nothing to cancel.
Do you work with integrators and security dealers?
Yes. Add monthly recurring revenue to every camera that you install. We run the service and it’s your name on the contract.
Who founded Verdun?
Verdun was founded by Sonny Tai, a former US Marine officer and the founder of Actuate, and Tung Hoang, who holds a PhD in Applied Mathematics and built Actuate’s first gun-detection AI model.
Book a demo
support@verdun.ai
